output.explanation: Expanded session-io because Terminal storage and Exec execution hide substantial ownership below Surface. Its central diagram now separates persistent Termio state, the scheduling controller and execution-stack resources. Two peripheral diagrams deepen Terminal/Screen/PageList ownership and persistent-versus-transient Exec lifetimes, with explicit borrowing edges between them. ownership-core and session-render remain unchanged because their existing boundaries are focused. Checked the pinned checkout's initialization, teardown and worker paths. Source-backed refinements: Subprocess.deinit also calls stop; successful launch closes the parent's slave FD only on POSIX; the gather pipeline is POSIX-specific; Kitty image storage is conditional; ScreenSet.active and cursor/page pointers are references rather than separate owners. All existing edges are retained, with moved IO endpoints updated.

Core Surface / IO ownership -- children own; -> borrows or hands off
|
|-- io: Termio [src/termio/Termio.zig:254-364]
|   |-- terminal: authoritative mutable Terminal [Terminal storage detail]
|   |   `-- Not owned by IO, render or search workers; survives their joins
|   |-- terminal_stream: persistent VT parser + StreamHandler
|   |   |-- Parser/handler state released by Termio.deinit
|   |   `-- -> terminal, mailboxes, size and renderer_state; processOutput
|   |       locks the shared mutex while parsing [Termio.zig:313-364,705-765]
|   |-- DerivedConfig, mailbox and startup thread_enter_state
|   |   `-- Entry destroys startup state even on error; deinit frees leftovers
|   |-- backend.exec: Exec [Exec lifetime detail]
|   |   `-- subprocess owns launch storage, PTY and process; not worker-owned
|   |-- -> renderer_state: shared mutex, terminal/inspector references
|   |-- -> renderer_thread mailbox/wakeup: scheduling and notifications
|   `-- -> surface_mailbox: borrowed route via CoreApp mailbox to this Surface
|
|-- io_thread: controller [src/termio/Thread.zig:44-136]
|   |-- Event loop, stop handle and callback completions
|   |-- Scroll, resize-coalescing and synchronized-output reset timers
|   `-- -> io / terminal / mailbox: passed to execution, no second terminal
`-- io_thr: OS thread handle; Surface spawns and joins it
    `-- Execution stack: CallbackData.data = Termio.ThreadData
        |-- backend.exec: transient Exec.ThreadData [Exec lifetime detail]
        |   `-- Owns watcher, write resources, timer and reader-thread handle
        `-- -> controller loop, Termio mailbox and shared renderer_state

Thread entry initializes stack state; return calls threadExit then data.deinit.
[src/termio/Thread.zig:259-285; src/termio/Termio.zig:367-428,830-851]

[src/Surface.zig:829-856] Terminal/parser outlive all reader/gather execution.

Teardown [src/Surface.zig:829-876]
Stop/join search, renderer, IO; then renderer.deinit closes display link,
then renderer_thread.deinit frees callback handles. Shared mutex/preedit and
final font lease survive worker shutdown; the app device survives all renderers.

Termio.terminal -- authoritative state, not a worker-owned snapshot
[src/terminal/Terminal.zig:49-106,344-404]
|
|-- screens: ScreenSet [src/terminal/ScreenSet.zig:23-112]
|   |-- all[key]: allocated Screen objects
|   |   |-- Primary created immediately; alternate created by getInit
|   |   `-- Each Screen [src/terminal/Screen.zig:45-87,315-367]
|   |       |-- pages: PageList -- active rows and scrollback
|   |       |   |-- Page/node/pin pools and live page list
|   |       |   |-- Tracked-pin set, viewport state, scrollback limits
|   |       |   |-- Page serial/epoch and incremental compression state
|   |       |   `-- deinit releases pin map, pages/nodes, then pools
|   |       |       [src/terminal/PageList.zig:401-487,978-988]
|   |       |-- cursor: position, style and optional heap hyperlink
|   |       |   |-- Cursor.deinit frees hyperlink and its allocation
|   |       |   `-- -> pages: tracked page pin, row and cell pointers
|   |       |-- saved_cursor, tracked selection, charset, keyboard protocol
|   |       |   `-- selection -> page pins; storage lives in PageList
|   |       |-- kitty_images: per-screen storage when graphics is enabled
|   |       `-- Semantic prompt, protection and dirty state
|   |-- generations[key]: incremented on removal to reject stale handles
|   `-- active -> all[active_key]; switchTo only changes the borrowed pointer
|       remove frees a non-primary Screen; deinit frees every stored Screen
|
|-- tabstops, title and pwd buffers; dynamic color palette
|-- glyph_glossary: session registrations
|-- kitty_dnd: optional allocation on client registration; destroyed on release
`-- Modes, dimensions, scroll region, cursor defaults and terminal flags

Screen teardown: Kitty image storage, cursor hyperlink, then PageList.
Terminal teardown releases screens and other owned storage; no worker owns it.
-> Shared access through Surface.renderer_state.mutex: IO parses/mutates;
   UI, rendering and search borrow this same terminal, not copies.

Exec branch -- persistent owner versus execution-scoped resources
|
|-- Termio.backend.exec: Exec [src/termio/Exec.zig:45-60]
|   `-- subprocess: Subprocess [Exec.zig:594-624,887-941]
|       |-- Arena-backed arguments/cwd and optional owned environment
|       |-- PTY: opened on threadEnter/start; closed by Subprocess.deinit
|       |-- process: fork/exec Command or Flatpak host command
|       |-- Grid/pixel dimensions and runtime pre-exec/post-fork information
|       `-- Successful start frees env; POSIX parent closes slave FD
|           deinit also calls stop before freeing PTY/env/arena
|
`-- IO execution stack: CallbackData.data.backend.exec = Exec.ThreadData
    |-- Optional process watcher + wait completions + exit/timing state
    |-- write_stream and write_queue
    |-- write_pool: pointer-stable Write objects
    |   |-- Each Write embeds request and 64-byte buffer
    |   `-- -> ThreadData: completion returns Write to pool
    |-- termios timer, completion and last observed mode
    |-- Reader handle and quit-pipe write end; borrowed PTY read FD
    |   `-- Reader execution: -> Termio, PTY FD and quit-pipe read end
    |       |-- Read end closed on reader return
    |       `-- POSIX reader stack [Exec.zig:1364-1520]
    |           |-- Pipeline: fixed buffers, ring metadata, mutex/conditions
    |           |   `-- Optional idle self-pipe; closed after gather joins
    |           |-- gather_thread handle: spawned and joined by reader
    |           |   `-- -> Pipeline / PTY / quit FD; publishes byte batches
    |           `-- Parse stage -> Termio.processOutput -> terminal_stream
    |               -> Termio.terminal: shared-mutex-protected mutation
    `-- -> Termio.ThreadData: controller loop, mailbox and renderer_state
        [src/termio/Exec.zig:86-230,493-566]

Shutdown: threadExit stops subprocess, signals quit, joins reader;
reader drains published batches and joins gather before its stack disappears.
ThreadData.deinit then closes write-end pipe and frees pool/watcher/stream/timer.
PTY and launch arena persist until Termio.deinit -> Exec.deinit.
Windows uses a separate reader path (no POSIX gather pipeline).
[src/termio/Exec.zig:196-230,549-566,887-892,1111-1133]
